question: Analyze the historical significance of the 'Cartaz-Armada-Cafila' system implemented by the Portuguese Navy in the Indian Ocean:
options: It was a peaceful cooperative trade framework that lowered transaction costs for Indian merchants.

It forced Asian merchant ships to purchase passes (Cartazes), call at Portuguese ports to pay customs duties, and travel in protected convoys (Cafilas) escorted by Portuguese armadas to prevent piracy and tax evasion.
It was a system designed to transport agricultural laborers from Bengal to the sugar plantations of Brazil.
It was a joint venture between the Portuguese Crown and the Ottoman Empire to blockade the Mediterranean.
explanation: Under the Cartaz-Armada-Cafila system, all local merchant vessels in the Indian Ocean had to buy a Cartaz, pay duties on their cargo at Portuguese custom-houses (like Goa or Malacca), and sail in organized fleets (cafilas) escorted by the Portuguese navy. Ships sailing without a license were liable to be seized and their crews executed.
